# Malt and fermentable substitution groups
# status: DRAFT. Written from general brewing knowledge as relationships between named items. Not copied from, and not
# verified against, the reference sites; spot-check lines against them and flip the last column to `reviewed`.
# compare against: brew.is malt guide, Wild About Hops malt substitutes (both blocked to scripts; open in a browser)
#
# line format: id | members (separated by ;) | tier | what changes | review
# tier: close = near drop-in | fair = same role, noticeable difference | distant = last resort | never = do NOT swap
# members are names, brands and aliases in English, German and Latvian so a case-insensitive search for any hits the line.
# colour numbers are EBC (EBC ~ SRM x 1.97). Search with: grep -i "<name>" knowledge/malt.md
#
M-PILS | Pilsner; Pilsen; Pils; Pilsner malt; Lager malt; Pale Lager; Heidelberg; NP Ultra-Pale; Ultra-Pale; Pilsner Latmalt; BestMalz Pilsen; Fuglsang Pilsner; Swaen Lager; Castle Pilsen; Pilzenes iesals | close | same role and colour (about 2-4 EBC); maltster differences are small, only mild flavour change | draft
M-PILS-DIST | Whisky Light; Château Whisky Light; Distilling; Swaen Distilling; Distillers malt; Pilsner; Pale Lager | fair | very pale (about 3 EBC) base malts made for distilling; high in enzymes and clean, usable as a base malt but read the label (some are low-smoke or peated) | draft
M-PALEALE | Pale Ale malt; Pale Ale; Pale malt; Two-row pale; 2-row; Golden Promise; Maris Otter; Halcyon; English pale ale malt | fair | about 5-7 EBC; more bread and biscuit than pilsner, slightly darker beer | draft
M-PILS-PALE | Pilsner; Pale Ale malt; Maris Otter; Golden Promise | fair | pilsner and pale ale malt can stand in for each other as base malt; expect +2-4 EBC and a maltier profile going from pilsner to pale ale | draft
M-VIENNA | Vienna; Vienna malt; Wiener; Vīnes iesals; BestMalz Vine; Swaen Vienna | close | about 6-10 EBC; toasty and light biscuit | draft
M-VIENNA-MUNICH | Vienna; Light Munich; Munich I; Minhene; Minhenes iesals | fair | Munich is darker and maltier; use less of it or accept a deeper colour | draft
M-MUNICH | Munich; Munich malt; Münchner; Muenchen; Minhene; Minhenes iesals; Latmalt Minhenes; BestMalz Minhene; Swaen Minhene Tumsa; Dark Munich; Munich II | close | about 15-25 EBC; rich bread crust; colour band matters more than brand | draft
M-WHEAT | Wheat malt; Weizenmalz; Pale wheat; Wheat; Kviešu iesals; Latmalt Kviesu; BestMalz Heidelberg Kvieši; Swaen Kviesu; Graudzēts kviešu iesals | close | about 3-5 EBC; head retention and haze, high protein | draft
M-WHEAT-SPELT | Wheat malt; Spelt malt; Speltas; Swaen Speltas; Dinkelmalz; Spelta iesals | fair | spelt malt is close to wheat malt with a nuttier flavour; similar colour (5-10 EBC), similar haze and body | draft
M-WHEAT-UNMALTED | Wheat malt; Flaked wheat; Torrified wheat; Raw wheat; Wheat flakes; Kviešu pārslas | distant | unmalted wheat has no enzymes and needs a mash with enough diastatic base malt; haze and body, less flavour | draft
M-CARAPILS | Carapils; Carafoam; Cara-Pils; Dextrin malt; Dextrin; Dextrine; Caramel Pils; Swaen Dextrin; Platinum Dextrin; BestMalz Caramel Pils; Chit malt; Swaen Chit | close | body and foam with almost no colour (2-7 EBC) and no caramel flavour; chit malt (unkilned) does the same job gently | draft
M-CARA-LIGHT | Caramel Hell; Carahell; Cara Hell; Crystal 10; Crystal 20; Light crystal; Caramel Light; Cara Gold; Swaen Gold Light; Gold Swaen Light; Belge; Gold Swaen Belge; Rudzu karamele; RedX; BestMalz RedX | fair | 10-50 EBC; light honey and caramel; RedX adds a reddish tint with mild flavour; swap by colour band | draft
M-CARA-AMBER | Caramel Amber; Cara Amber; Crystal 40; Crystal 60; Cara Aroma; Dzintara karamele; Amber caramel; Swaen Amber; Swaen Dzintara; Caramel Aromatic; Gold Swaen Dzintara; Melany; Sarkanā karamele; Caramel Munich I; Caramel Munich II; Cara Honey; Château Cara Honey; Château Arome; Klasiskais; Gold Swaen Klasiskais | fair | 40-130 EBC; toffee and bread; match the colour range first | draft
M-CARA-DARK | Caramel Munich III; Crystal 120; Crystal 150; Dark crystal; Cara Dark; Dark caramel; Gold Swaen Tumšās Minhenes; Karamele tumša; Gold Swaen Brown; Swaen Brown | fair | 130-240 EBC; dark fruit and burnt sugar | draft
M-SPECIALB | Special B; Special X; Special Belge; Belgian caramel dark; Caramel Aroma 300; Swaen Aroma; Gold Swaen Aroma; Super Brūnā karamele | fair | 250-450 EBC; raisin, plum, burnt sugar; strong flavour so keep the percentage | draft
M-BISCUIT | Biscuit; Biscuit malt; Victory; Aromatic malt; Melanoidin; Honey malt; Brumalt; Medus biskvīts; Swaen Honey Biscuit; Black Swaen Medus Biskvits; Stroopwafel; Platinum Swaen Stroopwafel | fair | bread, toast, honey and caramel-waffle notes (20-80 EBC); melanoidin and aromatic malts add maltiness, victory and biscuit add dry toast | draft
M-CHOCOLATE | Chocolate malt; Pale chocolate; Šokolādes iesals; Šokolāde; BestMalz Chocolate; Black Swaen Sokolade; Chocolate wheat; Chocolate rye | fair | 600-1000 EBC (pale chocolate 200-400); cocoa and coffee; wheat or rye versions are softer | draft
M-BLACK | Black malt; Black Patent; Black Barley malt; Melnais iesals; BestMalz Black; Carafa; Carafa Special; Carafa II; Carafa III; Black Swaen; Melnie mieži; Extra dark | fair | 1000-1400 EBC; carafa (de-husked) is smoother and less acrid than black patent | draft
M-ROASTBARLEY | Roasted barley; Roast barley; Roasted unmalted barley; Black Barley; Grauzdēti mieži; Black malt | distant | unmalted roast gives a drier, sharper coffee bite than black malt; keep the amount modest | draft
M-ROAST-COFFEE | Coffee malt; Kafijas iesals; Black Swaen Kafijas; Chocolate malt; Pale chocolate | fair | 500-800 EBC; coffee and cocoa; nearest to chocolate malt | draft
M-ACID | Acidulated malt; Acidulated; Sauermalz; Sour malt; Sauer; Rūgstošais iesals; Platinum Swaen Sauer; Swaen Sauer-skabais; Acid malt | close | lowers mash pH by lactic acid; pale and low in flavour | draft
M-ACID-LACTIC | Acidulated malt; Acidulated; Lactic acid; Lactic acid 80%; Pienskābe | fair | a liquid lactic acid addition can replace acid malt for pH, but contributes no grain; use a mash pH tool to size it | draft
M-SMOKED | Smoked malt; Rauchmalz; Beechwood smoked; Cherry smoked; Cherry Ember; Château Smoked; Kūpināts iesals; BestMalz Smoked; Peat smoked | fair | smoke type changes character: beech is mild and bacon-like, cherry is sweet and fruity, peat is phenolic and harsh | draft
M-RYE | Rye malt; Roggenmalz; Rudzu iesals; Crisp Rye; Rye | fair | spicy and dry; malted rye is easier to mash than flaked | draft
M-RYE-FLAKED | Rye malt; Flaked rye; Rye flakes; Rudzu pārslas | distant | flakes are unmalted and add silky body with less rye spice | draft
M-OATS | Flaked oats; Oat flakes; Rolled oats; Quick oats; Auzu pārslas; Oats flaked; Briess flaked oats; Instant oats | close | creamy body and haze; all are unmalted oats, pre-gelatinised | draft
M-OATMALT | Flaked oats; Oat malt; Naked oat; Naked oat malt; Swaen Naked oat; Hulless oat malt | distant | malted oats have enzymes and a different flavour; body is similar but less pronounced | draft
M-FLAKED-BODY | Flaked oats; Flaked wheat; Flaked barley; Torrified wheat; Torrified barley; Auzu pārslas; Kviešu pārslas; Miežu pārslas | fair | all add body and head retention without colour; oats are smoothest, barley is grainy, wheat is hazier | draft
M-ADJ-STARCH | Flaked maize; Flaked corn; Corn; Flaked rice; Rice flakes; Rice hulls; Kukurūzas pārslas; Rīsu pārslas; Maize | fair | maize and rice lighten body and flavour; they are fermentable adjuncts, while rice HULLS are only a lauter aid and never a substitute | draft
M-RICEHULLS | Rice hulls; Rīsu sēnalas | never | lauter aid, adds no fermentables; not a substitute for flaked rice | draft
M-DME-LIGHT | Dry malt extract; DME; Extra Light DME; Light DME; Spraymalt; Sausais iesala ekstrakts; Muntons Extra Light | close | about 98% solids; swap between brands by colour | draft
M-LME-DME | Liquid malt extract; LME; Šķidrais iesala ekstrakts; Dry malt extract; DME | fair | liquid extract is roughly 80% solids so use about 1.2 times the dry weight; check pack figures | draft
M-SUGAR-SIMPLE | Dextrose; Glucose; Corn sugar; Glikoze; Brewing sugar; Cane sugar; Sucrose; Cukurs | close | all ferment out fully and thin the body; sucrose is slightly less neutral than dextrose | draft
M-SUGAR-CANDI | Candi sugar; Belgian candi; Candi syrup; Dark candi; Kandīts | distant | dark candi adds raisin and caramel, clear candi is just sugar; not a flavour match for plain sugar | draft
M-LACTOSE | Lactose; Milk sugar; Laktoze | never | not fermentable by brewer's yeast; sweetness only; never swap with fermentable sugars or the gravity and sweetness change completely | draft
M-MALTODEXTRIN | Maltodextrin; Maltodekstrīns; Brew Body; Carapils; Dextrin malt | distant | maltodextrin adds unfermentable body with no flavour or colour; carapils is a malt that adds body and foam; they are not the same strength | draft
M-KIT-LAGER | Muntons Premium Lager; Premium American Light Lager; Mexican Cerveza; Zelta Lāgers; Crossman's Gold Lager; Lucid Pilsner; Iesala ekstrakts Pilsner | fair | pale lager-style kits and extracts; they differ in bitterness and supplied yeast; read the pack | draft
M-KIT-DARK | Connoisseurs Nut Brown Ale; Export Stout; Imperial Stout; English Porter; Brewferm English Porter | fair | dark ale-style kits; stout and porter kits are the closest pair, brown ale is lighter | draft
M-KIT-BELGIAN | Belgian Dubbel; Belgian Tripel; Brewferm Belgian Dubbel; Brewferm Belgian Tripel | distant | strong Belgian-style kits; dubbel is dark and fruity, tripel is pale and spicy, so they are different beers | draft
M-KIT-BITTER | Premium Best Bitter; Best Bitter; Muntons Premium Best Bitter | fair | English bitter kit; nearest alternative kits are other English ale styles, check bitterness and yeast | draft
M-GRAIN-NEVER | Base malt; Pilsner; Pale Ale malt; Black malt; Chocolate malt; Roasted barley | never | do not exchange base malts with roasted or caramel malts; colour, flavour and enzymes are completely different | draft
M-HONEY | Honey; Medus; Honey malt | never | honey is a fully fermentable sugar, honey malt is a grain with sweet toasty flavour; not interchangeable | draft
